avoidance.name: Avoidance
avoidance.plain: Not looking, or moving on, so the question never really comes up.

wilful_ignorance.name: Wilful ignorance
wilful_ignorance.plain: Choosing not to find out, because knowing would make things harder.

dissociation.name: Dissociation
dissociation.plain: Keeping the meat on the plate separate from the animal it came from.

perceived_change.name: Perceived behavioural change
perceived_change.plain: Feeling that you don't eat much meat, or already eat less, so the problem isn't really yours.

humane.name: Humane meat
humane.plain: Trusting that this meat came from animals that were treated well.

derogation.name: Do-gooder derogation
derogation.plain: Pushing back on the person who raised the question, rather than on the question.

deny_mind.name: Denying animal mind
deny_mind.plain: Seeing the animal as less able to think, feel or suffer.

dichotomisation.name: Dichotomisation
dichotomisation.plain: Sorting animals into ones we care for and ones we eat.

natural.name: Meat as natural
natural.plain: Eating meat is simply what humans have always done.

normal.name: Meat as normal
normal.plain: Everyone around you eats meat, so it must be fine.

nice.name: Meat as nice
nice.plain: It tastes too good to give up.

necessary.name: Meat as necessary
necessary.plain: You need it to be healthy, so it isn't really a choice.

third_party.name: Third-party blame
third_party.plain: The farms, shops or government are responsible, not you.

outrage.name: Moral outrage
outrage.plain: Anger at other wrongdoers that makes your own part feel smaller.

behaviour_change.name: Behavioural change
behaviour_change.plain: Considering eating differently: settling the discomfort by changing what you do.

aware_justify.name: Awareness used as justification
aware_justify.plain: Knowing you're rationalising, and letting that knowledge settle it. Our addition, not part of Rothgerber's framework.

attachment.name: Meat attachment
attachment.plain: Feeling entitled to meat as a personal choice. From a separate measure, outside Rothgerber's framework.

arousal.name: Discomfort
arousal.plain: The dissonance itself: unease that arrives before the mind settles it.

neutral.name: No mechanism
neutral.plain: A reaction that doesn't point to any particular mechanism.

triggers.name: Reminder that meat comes from an animal

beats.home:
It's Saturday, late morning, and the week is finally over.

You've arranged to meet Sam for lunch at the Smokehouse, the barbecue place on Mill Lane. You've got half an hour, and it's a good day for walking.

There are two ways into town: along the high street, or through the Saturday market.
beats.leave: You lock the door behind you. The street is quiet: someone washing a car, a cat asleep on a wall, the smell of cut grass.
beats.toLunch: You're a little early. Mill Lane is narrow, and you can smell the smoker before you see it.
beats.afterLunch: You talk about work, and a film Sam keeps telling you to watch. Then Sam heads off, and you take the other way home.
beats.end:
Home again. You put the kettle on and sit down for a moment.

That's the end of the walk.

e1.title: Lunch with a friend
e1.scene:
The Smokehouse is warm and loud, with long tables and music you half know. Sam is already there and waves you over.

The menu is chalked on a board above the counter. It's short.
e1.reply:
Your food arrives. Sam has a bacon roll, piled high. They look at both plates and laugh.

“Look at us. We eat a lot of meat, don't we?”
e1.replyVeg:
Your food arrives. Sam has a bacon roll, piled high. They look from your plate to theirs and laugh.

“Look at me. I eat a lot of meat, don't I?”
e1.prompt1: How do you feel about what Sam said?

round1.src: Piazza et al. 2015; Graça, Calheiros & Oliveira 2015; Macdiarmid et al. 2016

round2.src: Piazza et al. 2015 (Study 1: “I was raised eating meat”)

round2.w: I don't eat that much, really
It's the weekend, it's a treat
It's my choice what I eat
I've been trying to eat less, actually
Shall we try a meat-free week?

e2.title: Butcher's window
e2.scene:
The high street is busier. You pass the bakery, a phone shop with a sale on, then the butcher's.

The window is bright and tidy. Trays of mince. Pork chops fanned out on white paper. A neat pyramid of sausages with a little flag: “Our famous pork & fennel”.

At the far end of the window, on a bed of parsley, sits a pig's head.

pre.label: Keep walking
pre.text: You keep walking. The smell of the bakery follows you for a few steps.

ladder.text: Up close, its ears are pale and soft. It has long eyelashes, almost white. A price card leans against its cheek.

Its eyes aren't quite closed. Between the lids there is a thin line of dark eye, turned towards the street.

Under the price, in neat handwriting: “Our own, from Hollins Farm. Six months old.”

e2.prompt1: How do you feel, looking at it?

round1.src: Kunst & Hohle 2016; Kubberød et al. 2002; Ruby & Heine 2012

round2.w: I don't need to see that
Pigs are meant to be really clever
Hope she had a decent life

light.w: Must grab bread on the way back

e3.title: Vegan stall
e3.scene:
The market is in full swing: honey, potted herbs, a stall of secondhand books. A busker plays something slow near the fountain.

Beside the fountain is a small table with a hand-painted sign: “Ask a Vegan Anything”. Leaflets, a bowl of free biscuits, a clipboard.

A volunteer about your age catches your eye and smiles. “Hi! Have you ever thought about going vegan?”

pre.label: Stop at the stall
pre.text: You stop. They wait for your answer, still smiling.

pre.label: Walk on
pre.text: You give a small smile and keep walking. The busker finishes the song.

e3.prompt1: How do you feel about being asked?

round2.src: Minson & Monin 2012; De Groeve et al. 2021

round2.w: It's just normal to eat meat
Don't tell me what to eat
round2.src: Monin, Sawyer & Marquez 2008; Graça, Calheiros & Oliveira 2015

round2.w: How long have you been vegan?
Plants feel pain too, you know
I don't eat much meat anyway
My family would never go for it
Do pigs really feel it like we do?
Where do you get your protein?
